However with the proliferation of Internet usage, networked devices, and tools to create, edit, re-distribute, and manage diverse content items, the problem of maintaining reliable metadata in directory services of media servers is very complex. In this paper we analyze existing metadata frameworks used by industry consortia, specifically UPnP (universal plug and play) and DLNA (digital living network alliance) and discuss fundamental problems that cause content directories to be populated with unreliable metadata. We propose alternative methods based on implicit metadata and user-generated tagging that improve availability of reliable metadata.

articleTitle: Architecture for a Home Media Network Based on PTP-IP Connectivity Techniques
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: PTP/IP functionality is extended to enable networked devices to be organized in a sequential media processing workflow. The additional device functionality necessary to support this network architecture is not unduly complex and the workflow organization can be readily described through an intuitive user interface. This research offers an interesting alternative to conventional multimedia networking.

articleTitle: Architecture of PRML Decoder for BD/HD DVD Compatible System
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A partial-response maximum-likelihood (PRML) decode system, which enables to read Blu-ray Disc (BD) and HD DVD, has been developed. This system integrates following two functions; a PRML decoder for BD/HD DVD readout at highspeed, and an improved adaptive equalizer for correcting HD DVD's arbitration.

articleTitle: Conditional Access in Blu-ray Disc MPEG-2 Transport Streams
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Conditional access in most DVD recorders today is non-existent. In some high-end DVD recorders, there is partial conditional access at title level. However, such mechanisms of conditional access are highly proprietary and have very limited portability. With the advent of the Blu-ray recorders, it is possible to achieve conditional access at variable levels, starting from the entire disc to just a few video frames. This paper discusses convenient and computationally undemanding mechanisms of achieving conditional access in Blu-ray streams.

articleTitle: Highly Efficient Transmission System for Digital Broadcasting Redistribution Services over IP Multicast Networks
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper proposes a highly efficient redistribution service for digital broadcasting including high-definition video and data over IP networks. A prototype system is implemented based on the proposed scheme, and its performance is evaluated.

articleTitle: The History and Future of DSPs in Consumer Audio Equipment-Part II: Emerging Areas and the Future
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The article provides a list of emerging and existing consumer audio equipment. The use of digital signal processing (DSP) with psychoacoustic methods is further discussed.

articleTitle: A Platform Independent Digital Story Authoring and Distribution Tool for Mobile Handhelds
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Digital stories are short multimedia presentations, often used to effectively describe personal stories. Recently they have gained popularity on the Web and in TV broadcasting. This paper presents the design and implementation of a digital story authoring and distribution tool for mobile handhelds. The proposed tool is created using JAVA micro edition (ME) in order to incorporate platform independence. It aims at providing the possibility of digital story creation and sharing on the move. The system consists of a MIDP 2 based authoring tool for easy and guided creation and edition of stories, a Bluetooth and Wi-Fi based distribution tool for uploading and downloading stories from and to mobile devices and a viewer for viewing the stories created in the device and those downloaded from a repository. The digital stories are created in SMIL format for compatibility with MMS and with multimedia players in mobile and PC platforms. The paper describes the design, implementation and system integration of the authoring and distribution tool and highlight the associated challenges.

articleTitle: Detection of Hierarchically-Modulated Data for Advanced T-DMB Receivers
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper proposes a detection method of hierarchically-modulated (HM) data for advanced T-DMB receivers by incorporating coherent detection. To enhance the estimation accuracy, both a coded decision-directed scheme and a moving average method are introduced. Simulation results show that the proposed method successfully detects HM data only if the SNR is secured above about 20 dB.

articleTitle: Write System of Blu-ray Disc Drive for Video Camera
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents the write system for a Blu-ray disc (BD) camera drive to write with PCAV (partial constant angular velocity) method. The system controls the write waveform of the power and the pulse timing according to the write speed and the temperature. The power margin and the symbol error rate sufficiently show high performance not depending on the write speed at high temperature.

articleTitle: Low Complexity H.264 Intra MB Coding
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The H.264 video coding standard is highly efficient and at the same time highly complex. The complexity of encoding is substantially higher than prior standards such as H.263 and makes H.264 video encoding on mobile devices expensive. The few existing encoding solutions on mobile devices restrict the features used there by sacrificing quality for complexity. Fast encoding algorithms are necessary to fully exploit the advanced compression features offered by H.264. In this paper we present a novel machine learning based approach to reducing the complexity of intra MB coding. The results show that machine learning has a great potential and can reduce the complexity substantially with negligible impact on quality. The results show that the proposed method reduces encoding time to about 1/3 of the reference implementation with a negligible loss in quality.

articleTitle: Development of a Packaging Storage Format for Electronic Comic Services with Metadata
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper, The proposed e-comic storage format for comic contents packages comic images with related information such as additional contents, bibliographic information, user information and related contents based on the ISO base media file format that facilitates interchange, management, editing, and presentation of comic contents.

articleTitle: A Novel Mobile Node Based on OFDM for Ubiquitous Networks
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper, we present a novel physical layer model for mobile nodes which are currently considered inevitable elements in ubiquitous networks. The physical layer model efficiently exploits the OFDM features and a new channel estimation scheme, which leads to the considerable improvement of the receiver performance in the ubiquitous environment.

articleTitle: Accessing of Digital Media Contents with DLNA Protocol in Conjunction with DSI WSTP Protocol
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper aims to demonstrate the usability of DLNA protocol and to extend the functionality of DLNA in conjunction with DSI developed patent pending wireless storage transport protocol (WSTP) to allow convenient access of media content at home environment.

articleTitle: Bandlets for HDTV Video Processing
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Summary form only given. De-interlacing, scaling, frame rate conversion, compression artifact removals are currently major video processing challenges to produce high quality images for HD TV displays. Recovering high resolution images from degraded or lower resolution videos requires adaptive geometric filtering and interpolation in space and time, at very high data rate. Finding appropriate image representations for geometric image processing is currently a fundamental research problem. We first review some psychophysic and physiologic models of human geometric visual processing. We then introduce bandlet bases, which are multi-scale geometric wavelets, constructed along space-time trajectories adapted to the video content. Applications to HDTV video processing will be shown.

articleTitle: Video Segmentation-aided VCR Support for P2P VoD Systems
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: VCR functionality is difficult to be implemented in a P2P VoD system, since it may give more server workload and fails some distribution paths. In this paper, we first analyze the user behavior of VCR interaction, and propose a video segmentation-aided P2P VoD System with VCR functionality. The simulation results show that our mechanism could reduce the server workload and improve the VCR performance at end hosts.

articleTitle: A Robust Symbol Synchronization Method for Terrestrial-DMB Receivers in Hierarchical Modulation Mode
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Recently, hierarchical modulation has been considered as a way to increase the payload data in terrestrial digital multimedia broadcasting (T-DMB) transmission systems. This paper proposes a robust symbol synchronization method for T-DMB receivers operating in hierarchical modulation mode. It adopts a timing error detector which produces a timing phase error at the OFDM symbol rate instead of the frame rate. This method thus results in the robust synchronization of symbol timing in the presence of a sampling frequency offset (SFO). The simulation results show that the proposed method outperforms the conventional one, especially at a large SFO.

articleTitle: A Bayesian Network-Based Deinterlacing Scheme
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper proposes a novel motion adaptive interpolation algorithm for video deinterlacing. We employ a Bayesian network, which provides accurate weightings among common existing deinterlacing methods. It successively builds approximations of the deinterlaced sequence by weighting interpolation methods. The results of computer simulations show that the proposed method outperforms a number of methods in the literature.

articleTitle: An efficient training sequence for channel estimation in ATSC 8VSB system
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The authors propose a new training sequence for the channel estimation in frequency selective fading channels. The proposed training sequence has advantages from the points of complexity, sequence length and the channel estimation performance over the PN511 sequence used in the ATSC 8VSB system.

articleTitle: A New Transmission System for the Advanced Satellite Broadcast
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: NHK is developing ultra-high definition TV system called "Super Hi-Vision" which has 4320 horizontal scanning lines. This paper presents the new digital transmission system which has high transmission capacity suitable for the future broadcasting services such as a Super Hi-Vision program, high-speed program download services and various data services.

articleTitle: Impact of Fast Motion Estimation Algorithms on Super-Resolved Video Sequences
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Super-resolution (SR) algorithms present the drawback of a high computational cost, mainly due to the motion estimation (ME) stage. A good choice of a ME algorithm is a key factor not only to obtain high quality video sequences, independently of their characteristics, but also to reach real-time performance. A comparative of different fast block matching algorithms (FBMA) is made in this paper in order to facilitate the election of the one which presents the best tradeoff between video quality and computational cost.

articleTitle: Opportunities for 3D on Blu-ray Disc
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The introduction of various types of 3D displays, the increasing availability of tools for generating 3D content and new coding standards for 3D has created an opportunity to introduce 3D for the mass consumer market in the near future. Optical discs (i.e. DVD, Blu-ray Disc) will play a role as distribution media for high quality 3D video. For this to be a success both stereo and image plus depth will have to be supported. By building on the work done in the MPEG organization this can be achieved in a backwards-compatible way with minor adaptations to the standard and implementations.

articleTitle: Wearable Accelerometer for Numerical Diagnosis of Human Walk Using DCT
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: We propose a numerical diagnosis method of a human walk using DCT (discrete cosine transform) of a wearable accelerometer data. We found an apparent difference between smooth walks and non-smooth walks. Our work can contribute to the improvement of people health with a walk diagnosis made by a portable machine.

articleTitle: Dynamic Scan Initiation for Re source Efficient Operation in a 802.16e Network
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper, a dynamic scan initiation scheme in a 802.16e network is proposed in order for a mobile station to avoid waste of resources while meeting given handover time. Using statistical analysis on the received signal strength, a mobile station can trigger a scanning process only when a handover is anticipated regardless of random errors in radio propagation environments.

articleTitle: Real-time Embedded Panorama Mosaic System for Digital Camera
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: We propose an embedded image panorama mosaic system which can operate in real-time in digital cameras or cellphone cameras. The users can check the panorama result as soon as all the images are acquired by the camera. The proposed system shows comparable performance to other PC-based methods.

articleTitle: A Temporal Error Concealment Method for H.264/AVC Using Motion Vector Recovery
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper, a temporal error concealment method for the H.264 is presented, which uses the high correlation between the motion vectors of neighboring blocks. By using the motion vectors of neighboring macroblock of the lost MB, the motion vectors of the lost MB are recovered. Simulation result shows that the proposed method yields better subjective and objective quality than conventional methods.

articleTitle: Content-adaptive Resolution E nhancement of Compressed Video with Encoder-Generated Side Information
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper we propose a technique to dynamically generate optimized filters for the resolution enhancement of compressed video. The filters are derived during the encoding and sent to the decoder for post-processing. By making use of the scene-level and pixel-level classification, we adapt the filters to both the global and local content. Our experiments show 1-2 dB gain in PSNR as compared to the state-of-the-art techniques with ignorable overhead. Furthermore, it also improves the subjective quality with sharper images and suppressed artifacts.

articleTitle: User Interaction And Random Accessibility Analysis For Multiview Video System
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Human-computer interaction (HCI) mode between terminal users and multiview video system (MVS) can directly affect the performance of MVS. User and video content factors to HCI mode are studied in this literature. Practical probability parameters are derived to evaluate random accessibility performance of MVS and multiview video coding schemes.

articleTitle: Combinational Spreading and Modulation Technique for Mobile Satellite DMB Services
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The satellite digital multimedia broadcasting (S-DMB) service has been launched and can provide high quality audio, video, and data broadcasting services to the handheld mobile receivers via the geostationary satellite. To cope with the interference caused by the multi-path fading, the current S-DMB system utilizes half of the Walsh codes. To make full use of channel resources in the S-DMB system, a combinational method of the spreading and modulation technique is proposed for use in the S-DMB system. Applying the proposed method of the unused Walsh resources, we can achieve the increment of the system capacity without degrading the service quality of the S-DMB.

articleTitle: Clear Focused Image from Macro and Infinite Images
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In implementation, the time complexity and the performance of image fusion technique influence practicability of the products directly. In this paper, we propose an original image fusion method based on image spatial-domain features.

articleTitle: A Non-Invasive Arterial Stiffness Assessment Instrument for Homecare
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper, we discuss the development of an easy-to-use non-intrusive arterial stiffness assessment instrument PWV-DVPE (pulse wave velocity by digital volume pulse easy). The instrument records the digital volume pulses simultaneously from both the finger and the ear. The time delay difference between the two digital volume pulses is measured. The PWV is calculated by dividing the difference of the distances between the finger and the ear by the time delay difference. We study 34 subjects (20 men and 14 women, 20 to 44 years of age) and show the good performance of PWV-DVPE for monitoring arterial stiffness. At home, only a few minutes is needed for conducting a self arterial stiffness assessment. Therefore, early self-monitoring of cardiovascular dysfunction and arterial stiffness can be easily and effectively achieved.

articleTitle: Provision of the Multimedia Service Framework in the Ubiquitous Home Network
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The paper proposes a methodology to provide the multimedia services framework to provide integrated multimedia services in the home network. To do so, we define the requirements of a home media server, and implement its functionalities as a gateway for establishing connections between the home and external networks. The home media server pursues not only the integration of home network middleware technologies that allow automatic control and sharing with various Consumer Electronics (CEs) and A/V devices, but also intended to provide context based intelligences to the multimedia services for the ubiquitous home environment.

articleTitle: High Quality Directional Audio System
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Highly directional audible sound can be reproduced by the nonlinear interaction of finite amplitude AM ultrasound waves in the air. Due to the nonlinear process, however, the reproduced audible sound does not quite match the level of the traditional speaker in sound quality. There are mainly two reasons for this, namely, high harmonic and non-harmonic distortions and -12 dB/oct dependence for the low frequency response. In this paper, new methods for improving the sound quality are proposed and verified. Furthermore, a technique of forming desirable sound beam shapes is also discussed.

articleTitle: Flat hex Pattern for Large Range Fast Motion Estimation
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Fast motion estimations achieve reasonable computation power, by using search patterns to find a potential ideal match. This paper presents a flat hex fast motion estimation search pattern, which favors horizontal displacement over vertical displacement. Experimental results show that due to the enlargement of the horizontal dimension in the greatest conventional "circular" search pattern, the flat hex maintains similar PSNR, with a little reduced bit rate, but achieves a decrease computation time.

articleTitle: Development of HDD/D VD Hybrid Camcorder
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A new-type camera, HDD/DVD hybrid camcorder, was proposed, whose advantages are; (1) long-time recording on built-in HDD, (2) disc interoperability with DVD players, and (3) stand-alone dubbing function (times2 speed). The new camera, actually developed cost-effectively, is already in the market. This paper presents technically how the HDD/DVD hybrid camcorder was designed effectively.

articleTitle: A Hands-Free Unit with Noise Reduction by Using Adaptive Beamformer
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents an implementation of adaptive beamformer in a hands-free unit. The proposed adaptive beamformer suppresses stationary noise and interference sound. The adaptive beamformer and acoustic echo canceller were implemented in a compact hands-free unit with a low-cost DSP. The experimental results demonstrate the noise reduction performance of the hands-free unit.

articleTitle: Image Orientation Detection Based on Camera-subject Distances by Adaptive Control of Conditional Probability
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper, we propose a method of image orientation detection based on camera-subject distances. This method is characterized as an adaptive control of probabilistic decision by subject distances. The control is operated by switching of conditional probabilities of visual features at each subject distance category. The subject distance can be extracted from Exif. Evaluation and comparison is performed on 1681 consumer images. The experimental results show accuracy improvements on all visual feature combinations with negligible computational cost.

articleTitle: Applying Data Carousel to Improve Search Efficiency in P2P System
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper studies file-sharing P2P application among set-top boxes in bidirectional CATV networks. We try to find convergence between data broadcasting and P2P download. We use data carousel completes search work in P2P system. Finally, the experiments demonstrate advantages of the proposed strategy in hybrid P2P system.

articleTitle: DVB-H Key Management System for UMTS Capable Devices
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper we present a system to enable pay-per- view services in mobile handhelds which takes benefits of both DVB-H and UMTS networks. DVB-H infrastructure provides a more appropriate content delivery framework that UMTS. Despite this fact, UMTS can play an important role for charging and key distribution for pay-per-view applications by means of the provider SIM smart card.

articleTitle: A BD Camera with One-H our HD Video Recording
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A Blu-ray disc (BD) camera was developed with high definition (HD) video technologies; (1) 5 mega pixel CMOS imager, (2) H.264 video codec, and (3) BD compatible recording. The BD camera enables one-hour HD video recording.

articleTitle: Enhancement of 3D Shape in 2D Natural Images using a Non-Photorealistic Shading Approach
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents a non-photorealistic shading approach to enhance 3D shape appearance given in 2D natural images that do not have depth information. The approach is based on estimating and controlling normals on areas having relatively gentle shapes. Experimental results show effective and natural enhancement of 3D shapes, or improvement in 3D appearance.

articleTitle: Digital On-Channel Repeater for Terrestrial Digital Multimedia Broadcasting (T-DMB)
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: For T-DMB service, it requires a relay system such as the digital on-channel repeater which is usually called gapflller to deal with radio wave shadowing region and additional coverage. In this paper, we propose a new architecture of T-DMB gapflller and algorithms for the proposed architecture.

articleTitle: Meeting the Challenges of Digital Convergence on CE Platforms
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Presents the keynote address from the conference proceedings.

articleTitle: A Study on Cooperative Reception of One Segment ISDB-T
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Because of its narrow band characteristic, one segment ISDB-T reception is more degraded under multi-path fading environments than 13 segments ISDB-T reception. Moreover, efficient diversity reception is difficult for its physically small size of the receiver. In order to overcome this problem, cooperative diversity reception between several receivers is proposed and its performance is evaluated.

articleTitle: ML Estimation of Time and Frequency Offset Using Antenna Diversity in OFDM Systems
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents the joint maximum likelihood (ML) time and frequency offset estimator exploiting antenna diversity in orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) systems. Redundant information contained within the cyclic prefix (CP) is used and furthermore, we propose a new correlation coefficient for ML estimation and can obtain diversity gain from several received antenna signals. The method is efficient in an environment having a low signal to noise ratio (SNR) and multipath channel by combining the received signals from antennas in an OFDM system. In this paper we demonstrate an example of ML estimation from two received antenna signal.

articleTitle: Development of advanced PVR based on TV-Anytime
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents PVR system based on TV-Anytime metadata. Based on the features of TV-Anytime specification, the proposed system allows users to be able to easily record TV programs and to conveniently consume them based on segment defined in TV-Anytime specification.

articleTitle: Global Timed-Release Encryption
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents a new type of timed-release encryption (TRE), called global TRE (GTRE). TRE aims to control the timing of disclosing information. A promising approach assumes that any participants can receive a time token broadcasted by a trusted agent. GTRE improves the tolerance to missing receiving time tokens without interaction between any participants.

articleTitle: Beamformer-based Acquisition in MIMO-CDMA Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper proposes the code acquisition scheme on a MIMO channel for preamble search in a MIMO-CDMA uplink system. The performance of a ML code acquisition technique based on transmit and receive beamforming is analyzed by considering the detection probability. The acquisition performance and MAT for a MIMO code acquisition system are numerically evaluated. It is shown that the multiple transmit antennas can give the code acquisition system a transmit beamforming gain and result in much better performance than the corresponding scheme with a SIMO case.

articleTitle: A Study of MPEG-2 to H.264/AVC Transcoding with Half-Horizontal Resolution
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper analyzes the performance of MPEG-2 to H.264/AVC transcoding to half-horizontal resolution. Both the quality of the resulting video and complexity of the system are examined in the context of next-generation HDD recording systems. Experimental results show the importance of motion mapping to maintain high picture quality and that quality improvement over full-resolution transcoding is possible. It is also shown that transcoding to half-horizontal resolution allows for substantial reduction in complexity.

articleTitle: Application Profiling in a Dual-Core Platform
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Open Multimedia Application Platforms (OMAP), such as 161x and 2420, are dual core processors with an Advanced Risk Machine (ARM) and a fixed-point Digital Signal Processor (DSP). The decision of issuing or not part of an application to be executed by the DSP core must be carefully made, because of both, the additional complexity related to the design process, and the time overhead involved with control and data transfer between the ARM and the DSP. In this paper, we introduce a methodology to assess the performance of applications which use both cores. The results of the profiling might be applied to help designers map applications to the platform cores.

articleTitle: MMSE Equalization with Weigh ted SNRs for DVB-T receivers
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: When channels are slow fading, the MMSE equalizer can be considered for DVB-T receivers without matrix inversion. However, incorrectly-applied SNR values may degrade the equalization performance. To solve the problem, we propose a MMSE equalizer with weighted SNRs by the magnitudes of the estimated channel coefficients.

articleTitle: Multi-view Video Navigation Using Motion Sensing Remote Controllers
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The goal of Multi-view Video Coding is to allow coding of multiple camera views such that the user has the freedom of choosing the view point. While there have been significant efforts in multi-view compression, the work on navigation has been limited. The biggest challenge here is in developing user friendly and intuitive navigation of multi-view content. We propose a system which consists of multi-view video player and a motion sensing remote controller. Motion sensing remote controllers became widely available with the introduction of the Nintendo Wii game console. The remote controller captures motion when waved and the motion information is used to change the views in multi view video applications. This system gives users a convenient way of navigating through the multiple views by waving the remote in the desired direction.

articleTitle: ICCE 2008 keynotes: Awards Luncheon Keynote and Closing Luncheon Keynote
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Biographies are presented of Ralph H. Baer, the Awards Luncheon Keynote speaker, and Grant Imahara, the Closing Luncheon Keynote speaker.

articleTitle: Enhanced Mitigation Scheme for High Power and Long Duration Interference in DVB-T/H Systems
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper introduces an enhanced technique for mitigation of high power and long duration interference in terrestrial digital video broadcasting (DVB-T/H) systems. The scheme assumes perfect knowledge of the interference position and duration. Reliability information concerning the interference is constructed first and then combined with channel state information to perform soft bit scaling in the DVB-T/H receiver. The performance of the new technique is evaluated in static frequency selective channels.

articleTitle: Real-Time Local Contrast Enhancement Algorithm for Video Cameras with Built-in Noise and Artifact Suppression
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: For real-time imaging with digital video cameras, visibility of details is very important to ensure user confidence. Many complex scenes require local contrast improvements that should bring details to the best possible visibility. However, local enhancement methods mainly suffer from ringing artifacts and over-emphasizing noise. We present a multi-window real-time high-frequency enhancement scheme, in which gain is a non-linear function of the detail energy. Our algorithm controls perceived sharpness, ringing artifacts (contrast) and noise, resulting in a good balance between visibility of details and nondisturbance of artifacts. The new scheme can be successfully applied to any class of video system that would benefit from contrast improvement.

articleTitle: A Novel Wind Noise Reduction for Digital Video Camera
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: We developed a novel wind noise reduction technology for a digital video camera. This technology, based on our newly developed "clear sound algorithm", reduces wind noise without deteriorating the sound quality. It mainly consists of a wind noise detector, a harmonic structure restoration module, and a MPEG4-AAC module.

articleTitle: A Dynamic Multi-mode Switching (DMS) Error Concealment Algorithm for Video Device Applications
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper, a new Dynamic Multi-mode Switching (DMS) Error Concealment algorithm for H.264 video device application is presented. The DMS algorithm focuses on H.264 intra-frames. The error concealment mode switching in DMS is dependant on the temporal/spatial correlation, edge magnitude, strength of the motion activity of the corrupted MacroBlock (MB), and the smoothness of the reconstructed MB. The experimental results show that the DMS algorithm can achieve significant gains in PSNR and therefore it can improve the decoded video quality.

articleTitle: Remote Control Generating Dynamic User Interface Corresponding to Audio Visual System Configuration
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper proposes the user interface of an audio visual system remote control. The proposed system judges the system configuration, displays optimized graphical user interfaces in HTML and feeds back to a touch panel. The control prototype was developed with an embedded micro processing unit for consumer use. Verification experiments were conducted and normal operation was confirmed.

articleTitle: Architecture of a Low-Complexity Non-Binary LDPC Decoder
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper, we propose a hardware implementation of the EMS decoding algorithm for non-binary LDPC (NB-LDPC) codes, presented in [4]. To the knowledge of the authors this is the first implementation of an GF(q) LDPC decoder for high order fields (q ≥ 64). The originality of the proposed architecture is that it takes into account the memory problem of the NB-LDPC decoders, together with a significant complexity reduction per decoding iteration which becomes independent from the field's order. The error decoding performance of the low complexity algorithm with proper compensation has been obtained through computer simulations. The frame error rate results are quite good with respect to the important complexity reduction. The results prove also that an implementation of a NB-LDPC decoder is now feasible and the extra complexity of the decoder is balanced by the superior performance of this class of codes. With their foreseen simple architectures and good-error correcting performances, NB-LDPC codes provides a promising vehicle for real-life efficient coding system implementations.

articleTitle: The Bridge Component for UPnP and Bluetooth for a Wearable Computing Environment
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Home networks in the future will be complex systems of the BANs (body area networks) and the PANs (personal area networks), and will be composed of various wireless devices. Therefore, the self-discovery protocols that serve to control and maintain these devices are crucial. This paper proposes a bridge service that extends the capacity of widely used and IP based UPnP discovery protocol to a non-IP wireless device (Bluetooth). The bridge service has been implemented in an NPnP middleware component for a wearable computing environment in the BAN.

articleTitle: RFID Connectivity with STB for Viewer Identification in IPTV
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents the application of RFID (radio frequency identification) to identify the viewer in IPTV (Internet protocol television). RFID reader developed connects serially with IPTV STB (set-top box) for authentication of viewer and service verification by identifying viewer tag wirelessly.

articleTitle: System Architecture of H.264/AVC Codec LSI for Digital HD Camcorder
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A single chip H.264/AVC codec LSI was newly developed for digital HD camcorder, which integrates a video codec, an audio codec, graphics, video interfaces, peripherals, a host processor, and an SDRAM interface. In order to realize low-power real-time receding and playing back system, the LSI uses a software-based codec architecture and a flexible SDRAM control architecture.

articleTitle: Low-Complexity Linear-Feedback Equalization for ATSC DTV
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents simulation results of a linear feedback equalizer (LFE) for use in Advanced Television Systems Committee digital television receivers. Superior perceived performance compared with a decision feedback equalizer is observed under realistic reception conditions. A low-complexity implementation of the LFE is proposed: a novel hard-limited stop-and-go algorithm generates the error signal used for Feintuch coefficient updates. Favorable performance characteristics are confirmed through simulations.

articleTitle: Personal Interactive Bipedal Sym metry Re - education System to Aid the Recovery of Stroke Victims
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper describes a low cost portable system which allows stroke victims to improve their bipedal symmetry. The system measures the pressure distribution on the patients feet and encourages them to develop a full range of motion, using the pressure data as input into a simple game on the patient's PDA. This provides the patient with a valuable learning tool in the home, allowing them to lessen their performance deficit.

articleTitle: A DVB-MHP to Blu-ray transcoding scheme for interactive data
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Despite the similarities between DVB-MHP based Interactive TV and the new Blu-ray format, there still there exist substantial differences that make the two systems incompatible. In this paper we analyze the differences in both formats and propose a scheme to convert live broadcast interactive TV to the Blu-ray player system.

articleTitle: Behaviors-based User Profiling and Classification-based Content Rating for Personalized Digital TV
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper proposes a system embedded within digital TVs that aims at TV program recommendation based on descriptive metadata collected from versatile sources. The proposed system comprises a user profiling subsystem identifying user preferences and a user agent subsystem performing content rating. For intelligent implicit TV profiling, a novel scheme for observable TV user behaviors is developed based on linear regression. Furthermore, a new relation-based similarity measure is suggested to improve categorized TV program rating precision. The experimental results show that the content rating precision is enhanced enough by the proposed schemes.

articleTitle: A Reference Monitor Model for Improving User Comfort and Privacy of Home Gateway in OSGi Service Platform
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In home network environments, user comfort, and privacy are very important issues that need to be addressed. The reference monitor is the collection of access controls for devices, files, memory, and other kinds of objects and it is also able to provide advanced facilities for access control. In order to meet the user's requirements for comfortability and privacy, a reference monitor model is proposed for improving the home gateway in the OSGi service platform. The proposed model is based on the RBAC model, and the policy is classified into two types: user-role assignment policy and permission-role assignment policy. The policies are in XML format. With the use of the proposed reference monitor model, more effective guidelines can be provided for user access control in home networks.

articleTitle: Text-Independent Speaker Iden tification using Soft Channel Selection in a Multi-Microphone Environment
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: With the aim of improving speaker identification in a multi-microphone environment, we develop a text-independent speaker identification system. It incorporates soft channel selection before the combination of the identification results obtained by multiple microphones. The results demonstrate that the proposed system achieves high classification accuracy, thereby providing a speech interface for a wide range of potential hands-free applications in a ubiquitous environment.

articleTitle: Hardware Dedicated Integer-Pel Motion Estimator for High Definition H.264/AVC Video Encoder
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents a hardware oriented algorithm and its architecture of an integer-pel motion estimation for H.264/AVC. Proposed motion estimation architecture has a capability of real-time processing for 1080@60P with 2 reference frames and a search range of [-2048, +2047] in the horizontal and [-64, +63] in the vertical direction at the operating frequency of 266 MHz.

articleTitle: A Hybrid System That Support s Pull-type And Push-type AV Content Streaming Based on DLNA Technologies
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: We present a new system model based on DLNA 2- box models. The proposed system supports pull-type and push- type streaming of AV content on the same device platform, which is not directly supported by DLNA currently. This system also provides a streaming-conflict avoiding mechanism and a dynamic pull-push switching mechanism.

articleTitle: A Generic Approach for Digital Clock Synthesis Used for HDTV/PC-VGA Receiver
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents a new approach for PLL based generation of clock signals. The idea is to provide a generic solution that can serve a wide scope of applications. The novel architecture provides virtually unconstraint temporal resolution. The partitioning between analog and digital building blocks enables easy transfer to fast developing CMOS process technologies.

articleTitle: System Design of Advanced Video Navigation Reinforced with Audible Sound in Personal Video Recording
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents an advanced video navigation concept based on a picture in picture (PiP) allowing combined rendering of fragments of normal-play video and fast search video simultaneously. Loss of audio during conventional fast search trick-play is eliminated, by adding the sound of the normal play fragment. The normal-play fragments provide detailed information, whereas the fast-search signal presents a course overview. The audio associated to the normal-play fragments enhances the navigation process, allowing the viewer to concentrate on either the normal play or the fast search window. Efficient signal processing in the MPEG-2 domain permits re-use of the standard MPEG-2 decoding path for decoding the normal play audiovisual fragments. Applying a scalable MPEG-2 decoder for decoding the fast search signal enables a low-cost implementation for personal video recording (PVR).

articleTitle: A Model for Privacy Preserving Metering Service
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper, we propose a DRM system to protect users' privacy. The proposed system utilizes special protocols designed to preserve privacy using pseudonyms and an obfuscation mechanism. Those provide different levels of controls on metered data and personal identifiers, by expressing their preference on privacy sensitive information.

articleTitle: Interference to DTV Reception due to Non-Linearity of Receiver Front-Ends
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Terrestrial television broadcasting has always been an interference limited service. With the simultaneous transition to digital television and the reduction in RF spectrum, made necessary by demands for new wireless services, receiver design must give more attention than ever to mitigating interference. This paper will describe how receiver designs affect adjacent channel interference rejection and how interference from signals on what were once called UHF Taboo channels affect DTV reception and how such interference can be mitigated through suitable receiver design processes. Of particular importance is interference generated by signals on certain pairs of channels which falls in the desired channel as co-channel noise. This interference and that from a signal on a first adjacent channel is due to receiver non-linearity, usually occurring in the mixer.

articleTitle: Inter Mode Conversion of H.264 to MPEG-2 Video with Reduced Complexity
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper we propose an efficient inter mode conversion method for low complexity H.264/AVC to MPEG-2 video transcoders. The novel coding tools introduced in H.264 are exploited along with the more classic ones of MPEG-2, such that computational complexity reductions up to 60% and quality gains are achieved in comparison with full receding. The proposed method is suitable for software implementation of video transcoders in hardware platforms where the available resources are shared among multiple processes (e.g. home gateways).

articleTitle: A fast and efficient highlight detector for soccer
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents an algorithm to detect the highlights in soccer games. The algorithm was developed for use in embedded devices with limited memory and processing power. Simple video features are used to detect the play segments, whereas the highlights are detected by analyzing the audio power.
