articleTitle: Blu-ray Disc/DVD Compa tible Optical Slim Pickup for Video Camera Drives
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A blu-ray disc (BD) / DVD compatible optical slim pickup for video camera drives has been developed. In order to achieve both BD / DVD compatibility and the compact size, a dual objective lens method, collimator lens actuation for spherical aberration compensation, and shared front monitor (FM) were newly developed.

articleTitle: Directionally Filter Based Demosaicing with Integrated Antialiasing
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this document we disclose a technique integrating both a color interpolation method and an antialiasing method in a single step. This solution permits a reduction of memory requirement. In fact no extra memory lines are required to perform the false colors removal. This technique drastically reduces false colors and zipper effect by exploiting at the same time both spatial and spectral correlations.

articleTitle: Design of a Personal Cardiovascular Monitoring System with ECG and Stethoscopic Analysis
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents the design of a cardiovascular monitoring system, for implementation on an embedded device. Design of the necessary hardware is described, and ECG and Stethoscope analysis methodologies are detailed. A computational cost analysis is presented which shows implementation on a commercially available microcontroller is feasible.

articleTitle: Palmprint Alignment for Consumer Applications
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Biometrics such as fingerprint and speech analysis has been widely used for applications like owner recognition for consumer products (e.g. personal computers) and applications such as online transactions. Palmprint analysis is a relatively less studied area of biometrics that has consumer applications in both the traditional domain of identification/authentication and palmistry, which may be of interest to segments of the society. This paper presents an image processing technique for palmprint alignment that is applicable to both types of applications.

articleTitle: Frame Error Concealment Technique Using Adaptive Inter-Mode Estimation for H.264/AVC
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Since H.264/AVC achieves a high compression ratio by reducing spatio-temporal redundancy in video sequences, the payload of a single packet can often contain a whole frame encoded by H.264/AVC. Therefore, the loss of a single packet does not only cause the loss of a whole frame, but also produce error propagation. In this paper, we propose a novel whole frame error concealment method using adaptive inter-mode estimation for H.264/AVC. Experimental results show that the proposed method exhibits the better PSNR performance as compared with conventional methods.

articleTitle: Metrics to Evaluate The Quality of Motion Compensation Systems in De-interlacing And Up-conversion Applications
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Although motion compensation has improved a lot on natural videos, it still fails on sequences with erratic motions or mixed film-video content. This paper presents metrics to evaluate blur, combing artifacts, blockiness, halos and judder that remain typical limitations on such material even with state-of-the-art fallback policies.

articleTitle: User Interface Using Quick Palm Motions with Integration of Input and Output
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This research paper concerns interfaces for compact appliances. It proposes a method of controlling compact appliances using palm motions with low specification microcomputers. First, the problems of palm motion detection in the past are discussed as the background to this study. Next, the causes of the problems, an improvement policy and a method of achieving the functions the authors required are discussed. Finally, the results of the verification experiments using T-Engine and its various applications are examined.

articleTitle: The Design and Implementation of a Stereoscopic Microdisplay Television
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The next frontier for HDTV is stereoscopic displays that enhance the viewing experience. This paper proposes an innovative method of creating a high-quality stereoscopic display utilizing a Digital Micro-mirror device and high contrast shutter glasses.

articleTitle: Region-based Overlay Multicast in Mobile Ad Hoc Networks
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents a new multicast scheme to improve the data delivery ratio by reducing the overhead for tracing the trajectories of moving group members. From the simulations, we show that our proposed scheme improves the data delivery ratio up to three times, compared with the previous schemes.

articleTitle: Novel Bridge for networking IEEE 1394 clusters via UWB over Coaxial Cable for HANA & AV/C Digital Multimedia Networks
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The 1394-to-coax bridge described here has been developed to enable digital multimedia home networks using the existing coax infrastructures as backbone for networking HANA (high-definition audio-video network alliance) devices as well as legacy IEEE 1394 (AV/C) digital multimedia devices which are connected to different 1394 clusters widespread over the consumer's home. The implementation is based in the future standard "Networking IEEE 1394 Clusters via UWB over coaxial cable" , currently in development. One of our main goals was to provide a platform which verifies this standard.

articleTitle: Color Image Assessment Using Spatial Extension to CIE DE2000
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A full-reference method of color image quality assessment using a spatial extension of CIE DE2000 and cortex transform decomposition is proposed. Our test shows that CIE DE2000 tends to overestimate the visibility of distortion without emphasizing structural information due to lack of spatial vision consideration, whereas visible difference predictor shows also its insufficiency in predicting relatively smaller differences. Inspired by VDP and previous S-CIELAB works, we try to extract the most important visible differences using the proposed approach, and the map of distortion resulted shows a better correlation to the subjective qualities.

articleTitle: Seamlessly Interconnecting Legacy IEEE 1394 Devices over UWB Network: The Mirroring Bridge
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Bridging IEEE 1394 buses is becoming important since it enables wireless connectivity. Unfortunately, existing bridging mechanisms, such as the IEEE 1394.1 bridge and the transparent bridge, have practical limitations. The former does not support interoperability with legacy 1394 devices and the latter requires a new hardware chipset for bridge implementation. We thus propose a mirroring bridging mechanism to overcome these limitations. It supports interoperability with legacy 1394 devices by emulating remote nodes inside a bridge and via packet address translation that can be implemented in software. We have successfully implemented the mirroring bridge mechanism and conducted extensive experiments. The average throughput of the mirroring bridge was 188.7 Mbps, which is 99.3% of the maximum throughput of the UWB network.

articleTitle: Analysis of FPGA Solutions for Baseband Processing in Multi Carrier Communication Standards for Consumer Applications
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The paper presents FPGA-based reconfigurable implementations of the OFDM processing core for several communications standards of high interest for consumer devices. The proposed solutions are analyzed in terms of cost, power consumption and flexibility and compared with state-of-the-art implementations in semi-custom CMOS technology and FPGA.

articleTitle: A Wavelet Interlaced Video Coding Framework
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A discrete wavelet transform (DWT) based codec with EBCOT/adaptive coding mode switching/low-band-shift (LBS) is presented in this paper. The adaptive coding mode switching is used for both intra- and inter-frame coding, respectively, to improve the rate vs. distortion (R-D) performance. EBCOT, the coding engine used in JPEG2000 is adopted in this framework because of its embedded R-D optimization capability which is most suitable for the application of a perceptual distortion measure (PDM). LBS is used for motion estimation (ME) in DWT domain, while context based MQ coding is adopted to code the motion vector (MV). The context design of MV coding is derived from H.264.

articleTitle: Statistical Approaches to Quality Assessment for Image Restoration
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper, we propose two novel (non- parametric) statistical measures of image and video quality. Both of these are based on the fundamental notion of singular value decomposition, applied to local pixel and higher order information derived from the data. These methods enable measurement of similarity between images, and the measurement of image quality without a reference. A possible derivative application of the latter statistical measure is to optimize parameters of the relevant restoration algorithms being applied.

articleTitle: Protection of Window Med ia Video by Faked FourCC
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: As content serviced for IP set-top boxes is mostly streamed over IP network, the existing hacking tools for IP network can be used to capture the streamed content. Until recently, most of the content serviced on IP set-top boxes have been MPEG-2 TS. But it is being moved to WMV, MPEG-4 or H.264 gradually because of the compression efficiency. In this paper, we propose a DRM scheme other than WMRM for streamed WMV (windows media video) content. Our approach is to design a DRM scheme independent to the existing WMV streaming server. It also can control the processing time of DRM considering device performance.

articleTitle: Providing Entertainment by Content-based Filtering and Reasoning in Intelligent Recommender Systems
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Recommender systems arose in view of the information overload present in numerous domains. The so-called content-based recommenders offer products similar to those the users liked in the past. However, due to the use of syntactic similarity metrics, these systems elaborate overspecialized recommendations including products very similar to those the user already knows. In this paper, we present a strategy that overcomes overspecialization by applying semantic reasoning techniques. Thanks to the reasoning, our strategy discovers huge amounts of knowledge about the user's preferences, and compares them with available products in a more flexible way, beyond the conventional syntactic metrics. The resulting reasoning-based strategy has been experimentally evaluated in the digital TV domain. Our results show: (i) enhanced personalized recommendations, (ii) computational viability, and (iii) much greater accuracy.

articleTitle: Real-Time Free Viewpoint Rendering System for Face-to-face Video Conference
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Face-to-face communication experience plays an important role in videoconference applications. In this paper, we propose view angle rectification and view synthesis methods to generate the preferred view at observer's side. The proposed free viewpoint rendering system achieves face-to-face communication experience for real-time videoconference application.

articleTitle: Fast Mode Decision in H.264/AVC Based on Fuzzy Logic
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In H.264/AVC video coding standard, it allows seven block sizes to perform the motion estimation/compensation. H.264/AVC standard also uses the full search to obtain the best performance. However, it spends a lot of computational time. In this paper, we propose an algorithm which adopts the fuzzy logic technique and edge energy information of the object to determine the most appropriate block size to do the motion estimation without searching all the possible block sizes. The proposed algorithm has the advantages such as decreasing the encoding time and reserving the picture quality.

articleTitle: Low Power Continuous-time Equalizer Adopting a Clock Loss Tracking Technique for Digital Display Interface (DDI)
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper proposes a clock loss tracking technique for detecting the loss over the channel. The continuous-time equalizer adopting this technique improves the stability of system and the accuracy of compensation. Experimental results confirm that proposed equalizer is suitable for digital display interface.

articleTitle: Statistical Analysis and Derivation of Intra MB Mode Decision Rules for MPEG-2 to H.264/AVC Transcoding
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper, the DCT coefficients from the MPEG-2 decoder are used for the intra mode decision of H.264/AVC encoder. Based on the spatial activity analysis with the coefficients, early mode decision method between Intra16times16 and Intra4times4 modes and the Intra prediction direction are proposed. The empirical results show that the proposed method reduces about 70% computational complexity reduction compared with conventional method at the slight reduction in PSNR.

articleTitle: A Recursive Trellis Decoder to A pproach The Shannon Capacity in ATSC DTV Receivers
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The decoding structure of up-to-date ATSC DTV receivers is well optimized, and it seems that 14.6 dB is the unbreakable minimum SNR in the AWGN channel. In order to approach the Shannon capacity we propose a recursive trellis decoder which uses reliable feedback data obtained by an RS decoder. The performance enhancement of about 0.8 dB can be achieved.

articleTitle: Design Considerations for a 3D-TV Video Coding Architecture
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents an architecture of an acquisition, compression and rendering system for 3D-TV. We show that the proposed system yields two distinct advantages. First, it achieves an efficient compression of 3D/multi-view video by extending a standard H.264 encoder such that near backward compatibility is retained. Second, a high-quality 3D rendering is obtained by appropriately handling occluded pixels. The current proposal allows a gradual introduction of cost-efficient 3D-TV systems.

articleTitle: Reducing IPTV Chan nel Switching Time using H.264 Scalable Video Coding
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper we aim to reduce the switching time for Internet protocol tv (IPTV) using H.264 scalable video coding. In preview mode, we transmit the base layers of several channels simultaneously and thus switch instantaneously between them. In watching mode, the base and enhancement layers of the current channel are both transmitted and full video quality is achieved. Experiments show fast channel switching with negligible quality loss in watching mode.

articleTitle: Distributed Space-Time Coding and Equalization for Cooperative Cellular Communication System
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper, a joint distributed space time codes (DSTC) and equalization technique is proposed for cellular communication system in order to obtain the advantages of MIMO system with only one antenna for each mobile user. The proposed scheme can reduce two time slots during the cooperation phase. Simulation results show that the proposed scheme outperforms the conventional DSTC scheme in terms of system capacity. And also it achieves the same diversity gain as the conventional DSTC scheme with time division multiple access.

articleTitle: Real-time H.264 Encoder with Deblocking Filter Parallelization
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Real-time H.264 encoding of HD video is still a heavy task for today's high-end PC processors. To improve the encoding speed, we introduce thread-level parallelism to our H.264 encoder. However, the parallelized encoder with slice-level decomposition sometimes causes observable artifacts in encoded image. We propose a new parallelization technique for deblocking filtering that can reduce the artifacts without degrading the parallel processing efficiency. Experimental results indicate that our parallelized encoder improves processing speed by a factor of 5.9 with 8 threads. This is achieved without any noticeable artifact. We can achieve real-time H.264 HD (720p 30fps) visual communication on a PC platform.

articleTitle: 4GOOD - Technology and Prototype for a 4th-Generation Omni-Purpose Optical Disc System
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Digital optical data storage has become firmly established through CD, DVD and their derivatives. Future mobile and stationary multimedia applications demand for ever higher storage density, even beyond HD-DVD and Blu-ray Disc with 50 GB maximum storage capacity (dual layer). While holographic recording is in the far future for the consumer domain, the 4th generation of optical storage is being heralded by a leap in technology. Within a European initiative in the scope of the EUREKA project MobileDRIVE and the project 4GOOD (4th-generation omni-purpose optical disc-system), funded by the German Ministry of Economy and Technology, the fundamental technologies are being developed for high-density optical data storage (60...100 Gbit/ inch<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) in order to achieve at least 200 GB on a 12 cm disc, or e.g. > 5 GB on a 3 cm miniaturised version (single layer). The contribution describes the technology objectives, challenges, concepts and project status in the key areas of disc development, drive including laser, optics, acceleration sensors for mobile operation, and signal processing.

articleTitle: Photographing for On-line Mobile Panoramas
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper proposes the automatic and semiautomatic photographing methods that take multiple images for producing a panoramic image. While a semi-automatic photographing method uses a guided interface, an automatic method uses motion tracking information. These methods are applied on a commercially available mobile device.

articleTitle: Watermarking for Content Aware Intelligent Toys
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Digital watermarking establishes a reliable side- channel within audio-visual content. In this work, we use this channel to enable content-aware toys, which react to watermarks present in the content In particular, we discuss how the specific requirements of this application, such as accurate action timing and low-cost detectors, are satisfied with a series of algorithmic choices.

articleTitle: Architecture of a Consumer Lab-on-Chip for Pharmacogenomics
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents the architecture of the electronic detection and data processing (analysis) part, of a lab-on-chip (LoC) device. The LoC consists of a microfluidics part for the sample preparation and hybridization, a micro-system part including the sensors for the hybridization electronic detection and finally a processing part for the data analysis and the consumer interface for results presentation. Consumers will use such LoCs for identifying the appropriate cluster of a pharmacogenomic medicine based on the gene analysis results and optimize the effectiveness of the drug or determine whether they belong to a group of patients who would suffer severe side effects.

articleTitle: A Reduced Complexity Double Correlation Algorithm for Frame Synchronization
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper, we propose a method to reduce operational complexity of the conventional maximum-likelihood based double correlation algorithm for frame synchronization. The proposed method is based on frequency-domain processing by fast Fourier transform and a corresponding observation length for full-size shift of training sequence. Simulation result shows that the proposed algorithm can achieve reduced complexity without any loss in performance.

articleTitle: Highly Efficient H.264/AVC Codec Technology for High Definition Consumer Applications
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents newly developed highly efficient H.264 codec technologies for high definition consumer products. An essential set of H.264 coding tools has been determined as a result of an image evaluation. In addition, a new binary arithmetic decoding algorithm was developed in order to achieve necessary performance on the minimal sufficient clock frequency. These algorithms were implemented in our new H.264/AVC high definition codec LSI targeting mobile digital appliances including an HD camcorder.

articleTitle: Prefetching-Based Mobile Dictionary
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A network-based mobile dictionary requires frequent accesses from a mobile device to a dictionary server for searching or downloading materials. In this paper, we propose a prefetching-based mobile dictionary to reduce the network communication cost. We first propose an overall working framework for the prefetching-based mobile dictionary. We then present a method of determining the amount of prefetching data for each of packet-based and flat-rate billing types. We also propose a method of determining the words to be fetched in the near future. Through experiments, we finally show superiority of our prefetching-based method.

articleTitle: Emerging eHealthcare Consumer Electronic Device Systems
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper reviews an ICT-enabled consumer-centric eHealth system infrastructure supporting emerging heath and healthcare applications, and identifies the role of consumer electronics devices in the eHealth infrastructure. The state of art and standards progress for current and emerging eHealth- specific consumer electronic devices will be discussed.

articleTitle: A New Edge-Based Intra-Field Interpolation Method for Deinterlacing using Locally Adaptive-Thresholded Binary Image
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Traditional edge-based methods for de interlacing were poor at determining accurate edge direction which decides interpolation performance. The proposed method decides the direction and slope of edge based on locally adaptive-thresholded binary image, and it also increased the horizontal size of search window for better performance.

articleTitle: Initial Acquisition for Next Generation MB-OFDM UWB Transmission
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: We present an efficient acquisition algorithm for a next-generation multi-band orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (MB-OFDM) ultra wideband (UWB) system. The simulation results show that the proposed packet detection algorithm which employs both an M-sample time delayed cross correlation value, and a received signal power calculated by using the received input samples less than zero padding (ZP) outperforms the conventional packet detection algorithms.

articleTitle: Error Tracking Based Error Concealment Strategy for Scalable Video Coding
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Scalable video coding (SVC) is a new emerging video coding standard to be released as an amendment of the H.264/AVC The SVC standard adopts four post-processing EC methods to cope with frame loss caused by transmission error. In SVC, however, there have been few studies on burst errors by which several successive frames are corrupted in noisy channels. In this paper, we first propose an error tracking model with which the concealment error and the propagation error can be estimated. Then, in order to cope with the burst error in error-prone networks, we introduce a novel error concealment (EC) strategy based on the proposed error tracking model. For each lost frame, the proposed strategy selects one of four EC methods adopted in the SVC that minimizes the visual degradation.

articleTitle: Secure Framework of Audiovisual Content based on Bi-directional Authentication for Hard Disk Drive
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: We have developed content protection technologies best suitable for hard disk drives. Besides large capacity and high speed, the hard disk drive has some better features than optical discs, one of which is intelligent enough to make bi-directional authentication to the system. This benefit realizes more flexible and reliable protection of digital content. This paper describes the total framework of the developed protection mechanism, focusing on audiovisual content which is used in a wide range of applications.

articleTitle: A Circular Buffering Algorithm for Hiding Channel Zapping Delay in a Digital Television
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper, we propose a new method for hiding the channel change delay by efficiently utilizing multiple tuners. One tuner is used to capture a channel being watched and the others are used to buffer other channels. In order to raise tuner usage efficiency, each buffering tuner circulates multiple channels and buffers the A/V stream. The channel change delay is hidden by displaying a buffered A/V stream during the channel change delay. Experimental results showed that the proposed algorithm gave higher user satisfaction results when compared with other methods.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Color Reproduction System for Images Captured by Digital Camera
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: We present the design and implementation of a color reproduction system for images captured by digital camera. In the proposed system, the color-target based approach is used, because this requires only a known target and is, therefore, a more practical method. The accuracy and robustness of the proposed system are verified on the experimental results of several indoor and outdoor images.

articleTitle: Efficient Architecture for Full HD 120 Hz Frame Rate Conversion
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Motion blur is one of the remaining concerns for LCD-TVs. A solution is provided by reducing the sample-and-hold time by driving the LCD-panel at a higher temporal frequency (120 Hz), and additionally properly converting the video signal into a 120 Hz video stream. Applying motion-compensated frame-rate conversion (MC- FRC) technology not only requires sophisticated algorithms but an underlaying video architecture as well which can sustain the high throughput rates, particularly for full HD at 120 Hz. In this paper, we present the algorithm and video architecture which enables the conversion of 120 Hz occlusion-free MC-FRC for up to full HD sources.

articleTitle: DSL Forum's Focus: Quality Delivery and Management of IPTV
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The full potential of IPTV can be achieved if the industry works together, developing and adhering to industry standards such as those discussed in this paper. The DSL Forum welcomes participation from equipment vendors, service and content providers and all other interested parties, and through liaison and joint work, reaches out to other organizations as well to ensure that strong end-to-end solutions are developed. As the Forum's scope continues to expand, incorporating access agnostic work and focusing on application service delivery, it stays aligned with the priorities of the industry and the needs of the service provider. To find out more about the BroadbandSuite initiative, upcoming meetings and interoperability events, global DSL subscriber information or about membership of the DSL Forum, visit www.dslforum.org.

articleTitle: A Proposal on Video Editing System Coping with Rights Inheritance Management for Secondary Content
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents a video editing system based on the proposed rights inheritance framework for generating a secondary content. We propose rights inheritance content editor (RICE) module that provides the editing control with digital rights management (DRM) according to the granted rights during the authoring process, and manages inherited rights generation for derived contents. With our proposed rights inheritance framework and RICE, a secondary content can be generated respecting the rights of original contents.

articleTitle: On De-Embedding Phase for High Speed Connectors
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The phase error problem in de-embedding is examined for board structures and devices under test (DUT). The main feature of this paper is the comparison between the S-parameter data for the embedded DUT and the data for a judiciously chosen reference situation. It is important to note that de-embedding the phase is essential in the design of high-speed connectors in consumer electronics hardware, especially in providing "swappable" models for high-end microprocessor-based applications.

articleTitle: Autonomic System Management for the PDA
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper describes the component-based autonomic computing system for the PDA or smart phone. The proposed method includes self reconfiguration and self-healing. The self reconfiguration provides the dynamic reconfiguration of middleware according to the upgrade of middleware components and provides efficient execution of the application by organizing the minimal set of middleware components. The self healing provides the system recovery and the re-installation of the application and middleware components against runtime errors from the applications.

articleTitle: Preserving Our Digital Heritage
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: All three present technologies for storing single copies of digital data (magnetic, optical, and solid state) are characterized by relatively short lifetimes, ranging from 5 to 30 years. There presently exists no inexpensive way to preserve one's digital data for posterity. This paper describes a research effort which is targeting 1,000 years (a millennium) for a new type of recordable optical storage.

articleTitle: Error Sector Inventory on Optical Disc for Defect Avoidance during Recording / Playback Digest of Technical Papers
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper proposes a method to create on-the-fly inventory of error sectors, so that subsequent recordings / playback are free from the audio-video hiccups and retries and still compliant with DVD-Video / DVD+RW logical standard. This will in-turn aid in creating good user experience (no audio-video hiccups) and helps in using processor MIPS efficiently (no retries).

articleTitle: Square: 3×3 Keypad Mapped to Geometric Elements of a Square
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: We introduce Square, a text entry device in the form of a small square button. Conceptually, it is equivalent to a 3times3 keypad since the nine geometric elements of the square - four vertices, four edges, and a face - play the part of the nine keys of a 3times3 keypad. Being small and simple, on the other hand, Square can allow more freedom to the design of a mobile device. In addition, it is suitable for blind typing due to the distinct tactile properties of the different elements of the square button.

articleTitle: A Musical Onset Detection System with Scalable Complexity
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: An onset detection system based on linear prediction with scalable complexity is proposed in this work. One unique feature of the proposed onset detection algorithm is that it can offer a trade-off between complexity and detection accuracy by adjusting its parameters. Consequently, it can be used in consumer electronics such as karaoke performance evaluation and automatic visual effect generation in portable media players.

articleTitle: Test Video Selection for Video Processing Research and Development
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Many video processing algorithms have been developed in recent years. However, visual performance validation of these algorithms is often overlooked. We discuss the need for a standardized suite of free test videos appropriately selected according to a set of usage rules. These videos are to be stored in a publicly accessible online library that will facilitate effective collaboration and interaction among research scientists and development engineers.

articleTitle: A Clustered Flash Translation Layer for Mass Storage CompactFlash Systems
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents a novel flash translation layer design that uses clustered hash tables and two-level software cache technique to adaptively switch logical address from the host system to physical address in flash memory. The experimental results show that the proposed address translation mechanism provides good performance in address mapping and memory space requirement over the well-known NFTL and AFTL.

articleTitle: Trick Play Method for HD H.264 Set-Top Box
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: We envision a mid-session control with 2-level speed scaling scheme that server can control content playback speed without client's aid. Also, our scheme doesn't need re-encoding, so server still can use well-known performance features. Therefore, it promises great advantages for set-top box makers.

articleTitle: A wearable health co ntext aware system
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper, we report upon the prototype development of a wrist-worn integrated biosignal measurement system-WIBMS-with a wireless-transferring function. The functional objective of the WIBMS is to provide information concerning clinical state, such as vital signals and motional information in activity, to experts at a distance. Thereby, the unit provides the facility for rapid and appropriate directions to be given by experts in emergency situations, and enables the user or the supervisor to manage changes in health condition with helpful treatment.

articleTitle: A Distortion Reducing Subband Limiter Implementation for Conference Phones
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Distortion, most often caused by the loudspeaker, is a practical problem in acoustic echo cancellation-based conference phones. Typically, this distortion varies significantly with the frequency. This paper presents an implementation of a distortion reducing subband limiter to be used in conjunction with an acoustic echo canceller in a commercial conference phone, yielding improved cancellation performance. Verification of the performance was performed through evaluation of a fix-point real-time implementation.

articleTitle: Device Control with Scriptable-API Using Web Based Framework
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents an advanced control mechanism to enable 3-box control in web based framework such as CEA-2014. Web-base control is a noble and user- friendly method to manage a home network device within web browser. However, current web based control mechanism only allows controller to interact with single controlled device. In this paper, we describe a mechanism to control multiple home network devices using web based control.

articleTitle: A Novel Design Approach for H.264/AVC Motion Estimation Architectures
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A new approach for exploring different allocation alternatives of the computational resources within H.264/AVC motion estimation architectures is presented in this paper. The use of this methodology has motivated the introduction of a novel architecture able to process CIF@60fps sequences with a reduced equivalent gate count and dynamic power savings.

articleTitle: A Front-end Signal Processing LSI for HD DVD/DVD/CD with Dual-Adaptive PRML
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents a Digital Front-end LSI using 0.13 μm CMOS for HD DVD/DVD/CD compatible drives. To insure sufficient readout performance in dual layer HD DVD-R/RW disks, the LSI is equipped with a dual-adaptive PRML feature. The experimental result shows that sufficient performance improvement has been achieved with this LSI.

articleTitle: On the performance of VoIP and IPTV over a Wireless Mesh Network in an Outdoor Environment
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Wireless mesh networks (WMNs) will play an important role in the next-generation wireless communication systems because they can support broadband services with ubiquitous coverage by low transmission power. In this article, we investigate and analyze the performance of service like VoIP and IPTV distributed in a WMN which is deployed in an outdoor environment.

articleTitle: Efficient Discrete-Time Bandpa ss Sigma-Delta Modulator for Multistandard Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents efficient discrete-time bandpass sigma-delta modulator for multistandard wireless applications. The proposed discrete-time bandpass sigma-delta modulator provides the higher speed by advanced switched-capacitor resonator which is about 50% faster than the latest reported ones, and it is also optimized to support multi-bandwidth for digital convergence applications. The proposed discrete-time bandpass sigma-delta modulator is implemented using a 0.18μm CMOS technology, and has an effective chip area of 0.16mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Estimating Inter-Frame Parametric Dominant Motion at 1000fps Rate
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: We present a very low-complexity method for estimation of parametric global motion in video. First, the motion is approximated by translation, then small peripheral blocks from the rectangular area of overlap are matched, and local motion vectors (MVs) are extracted. Both global translation and local MVs are efficiently computed using ID phase correlation of integral image projections. The global parametric motion is estimated from inlier MVs found by the RANSAC. Our main contributions, enabling high performance, are: 1) non-informative block rejection based on image projection analysis, 2) informative block search using line scanning from peripheral blocks towards the central block, and 3) iterative replacement of the outlier MVs. The achieved performance is ~1000 fps for CIF frame. The method is demonstrated in video sequences with rapid camera motion, zoom and rotation. Geometric and photometric comparisons with two other motion estimation methods are performed.

articleTitle: Global Illumination for Advanced Computer Graphics
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Real-time 3D graphics is present today on various devices, from high-end PC powered by highly complex GPUs to more simple handheld consoles or mobile phones. All these solutions are based on an aging technique called immediate mode rasterization, very efficient for rendering simple scenes, but unable to capture essential visual features such as soft shadows, indirect lighting, real reflection and refractions, caustics, etc. Only global illumination algorithms are able to render such features. Moreover, the rendering time of a GPU increases linearly with the scene complexity, whereas a ray tracing solution shows a logarithmic progression. The aim of this paper is to present an overview of such global illumination algorithms, their common theoretical background and the advancements made to execute them in real-time.

articleTitle: A Network Level Power Management for Home Network Devices
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper proposes a network level power management based on the energy-aware plug and play (EPnP) for home network devices. The power management can reduce the power consumption of devices by reconfiguring power control elements of each device depending on a service collaborating with many devices in the home network. It also can reduce the power consumption of devices without user intervention by EPnP technique. It can provide a power reduction at network level by a fine grain power control based on home network services.

articleTitle: A Hierarchical Mode Decision Method for The Fast H.264/AVC Intraframe Coding
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper, we propose a hierarchical mode decision method for intraframe coding to reduce the computational complexity of the encoder, based on the spatial characteristics. The simulation results show that the proposed algorithm achieves 20% to 50% reduction in the computational complexity compared with the conventional algorithms.

articleTitle: Intelligent 1-Dimensional Channel Estimation Methods and Its Application to DVB-T System
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper, we propose a channel estimation method associated with the interpolation order for DVB-T systems. We first analyze the time varying channel and frequency selective channels, and then derive the channel index which indicates the ratio of the time and the frequency axis variation. This channel index is used for determining the order of interpolation such as time axis followed by frequency axis interpolation or vice versa. The computer simulation shows that the proposed method can provide more accurate channel information, thereby improving the overall channel equalizing performance.

articleTitle: Development of Optical Disc Servo Simulation Based on Actual Waveform Data
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A new servo simulation method based on actual waveform data has been developed. The actual track displacement of an optical disc is calculated from a measured servo error signal using an inverse model of the optical disc drive. The simulation result well corresponds with the actual servo response.

articleTitle: Bidirectional Interactive Conten ts Player for Terrestrial Digital Multimedia Broadcasting (T-DMB)
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents a bidirectional interactive contents player for terrestrial digital multimedia broadcasting (T-DMB). The presented player is capable of sending user requests to a proper return channel server using information included in a scene presentation. The player provides functionality to combine requested data received via communication networks with the initially broadcasted contents to present additional information to users. The result of a request transmitted back through the broadcasting network can also be presented properly using the presented player.

articleTitle: Frame Boundary Detection for Full-Band Support in MultiBand-OFDM System
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents a solution for the frame boundary detection to support all band groups at the overall bandwidth of 3.1-10.6 GHz in the multiband-OFDM system. This solution is based on the sign variations of the autocorrelation outputs of the received signals according to the carrier frequency offset and covers the full-range frequency tolerance for all band groups.

articleTitle: Enhanced Transform Domain Intra Prediction for MPEG-2 to H.264/AVC Transcoding
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper, we proposed an enhanced transform domain intra prediction for H.264/AVC. In the proposed scheme, H.264 intra prediction can be described by generalized linear operation after defining both H-filter and V-filter. Since intra prediction operation can be decomposed into some sparse matrices, we can reduce computational complexity for intra prediction. Our scheme can reduce the number of multiplication and addition operations more than Chen's by 22.4% and 21.6%, respectively, in each 4 times 4 block. We can insist that the proposed scheme can be used for fast transform domain intra prediction in the area of transcoding MPEG-2 streams into H.264/AVC streams.

articleTitle: An Efficient Architecture for Hardware Implementation of H.264/AVC Deblocking Filtering
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper, a novel hardware architecture for real-time implementation of the adaptive deblocking filtering process specified by the H.264/AVC standard, is presented. The proposed architecture is based on a double-filter strategy that results in a significant saving in filtering cycles, memory requirements and gate count when compared with state-of-the-art approaches.

articleTitle: Performance of Ad-Hoc Wireless Network on 2.4GHz Band in Real Fields
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper describes the performance of ad-hoc wireless network on 2.4 GHz band in the real buildings and homes. The communication module based on the IEEE802.15.4 standard was developed and installed into four kinds of buildings with different structures. The attenuation of the signal resulting from obstacles in the real world and the coexistence of 802.15.4 with other products of the same radio frequency band were evaluated.

articleTitle: A NovelAudio/ideo Decoder for Video Recorders
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper describes an integrated audio/video decoder for video recorders. The IC has a number of novel features designed to improve video decoder performance over what is now available in the market whilst also introducing measures to reduce the implementation cost and the power consumption.

articleTitle: A Scheme for Location Transparent Access to Networked Consumer Electronics
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: These days, devices known as "networked consumer electronics" (NCE), are being manufactured with installed IP functions. If a fixed address is embedded in an NCE, control, maintenance, and monitoring of the device is facilitated. We propose a scheme to enable an NCE with an embedded fixed IPv6 address to communicate with any node through a collaboration of the NCE and a home network gateway. This scheme reduces the development cost and processing load of NCEs as well as the cost of managing IP addresses of NCEs by using fixed IPv6 addresses.

articleTitle: Efficient Retransmission Architecture of Digital Broadcast Services over IPTV Networks
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper describes architecture for supporting legacy digital broadcast services over IPTV networks. Legacy services refer to pre made real-time broadcast streams based on open standards such as MHP, ACAP, and OCAP. They use MPEG-2 TS as delivery protocol, but this is not a good choice for IPTV as it is defined in view of unidirectional media such as terrestrial or satellite networks. The proposed architecture retransmits digital broadcast services using IP-oriented protocols including service delivery, service discovery and selection, XML-based application signaling, and integrated application execution engines.

articleTitle: An Inexpensive Impulse Detector and Finite State Timing System
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper proposes a system that identifies impulses on flat rigid boards. Based on digital filters, it generates a trustworthiness trigger index that rules a finite state machine timer. The system has been done with an inexpensive 8-bit microcontroller bundled with switched capacitor technologies.

articleTitle: Asymmetric Bi-Directional Optical Fiber Module for High-Definition Video Transmission
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper describes a bi-directional optical fiber module that provides transmission of high-definition video and control signals through a single optical fiber. The optical fiber module uses a multiple-face lens with multiple optical surfaces, and contributes to the creation of an inexpensive, easy-to-use optical fiber transmission system.

articleTitle: Low-Cost Camera Motion Extraction in Compressed Videos
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper proposes a new algorithm of only using motion vectors (MVs) of macroblocks contained in MPEG encodings to fast extract camera motion directly from compressed videos. Due to very low computing cost, our algorithm is faster than real-time processing, and thus suitable for implementation on hardware, such as PTZ video camera.

articleTitle: Channel-Aware V ideo Streaming for Mobile Devices over WiBro Network
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents a channel-aware video streaming method that does not only adjust dynamically the target bit rate according to the channel condition but also minimize the error propagation at handoff. The proposed method performs adaptive bit rate allocation (ABA) by using the carrier to interference and noise ratio (CINR) to reduce the packet loss ratio (PLR) without wasting the channel resource. Moreover, adaptive intra refresh (AIR) is performed to reduce the error propagation when the handoff is occurred. Experimental results indicate that the proposed method can be successfully used for video streaming over WiBro networks.

articleTitle: Eye-View: A Retinal Image Acquisition System
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents a low cost but high resolution retinal image acquisition system of the human eye. The images acquired by a CMOS image sensor are communicated through the Universal Serial Bus (USB) interface to a personal computer for viewing and further processing. The image acquisition time was estimated to be 2.5 seconds. This system can also be used in telemedicine applications.

articleTitle: A DSP Based H.264 Dec oder for a Multi-Format IP Set-Top Box
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper, the implementation of a digital signal processor (DSP) based H.264 decoder for a multi-format set-top box is described. Baseline and Main profiles are supported. Using several software optimization techniques, the decoder has been fitted into a low-cost DSP. The decoder alone has been tested in simulation, achieving real-time performance with a 600 MHz system clock. Finally, it has been integrated in a multi-format IP set-top box using a commercial development board based on the DSP @ 600 MHz. Tests in a real environment have been performed using this board with good results.

articleTitle: Increasing the Number of Disc Overwrites on Recordable Disc
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper proposes a method to increase the number of times a recordable disc can be overwritten, in-turn the number of Disc Overwrites. The problem is that recordable disc, if overwritten several times with the exact same channel code pattern at the same physical address will become fatigued and will lead to permanent damage. This paper proposes a solution wherein the number of Disc Overwrites can be greatly increased at application level by insuring that at least one byte in a sector is different, each time that sector is written.

articleTitle: Improvement of Collision Detection Performance of Hierarchies by Using Classified Dynamic-Density of 3D Objects
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper, features of various collision detection algorithms for standard 3D objects among 3D graphic algorithms were analyzed, and a 'Classified dynamic density (CDD)' that utilizes the center value and corner points of standard objects in represent hierarchical structures is suggested. By using CDD, an Level-of-Detail(LOD) algorithm can be applied to 3D space to improve collision detection of 3D objects. Also, through suggesting efficient rendering of 3D spaces as an important element of 3D graphics and a realistic expression method, the realism and efficiency of 3D games can be greatly improved.

articleTitle: Globalization Trends in CE Design, Manufacturing, and Sales [Keynote Speech]
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Presents the keynote address from the conference proceedings.

articleTitle: A Low Cost and Fast Handoff Solution in IPv6 Networks
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: As the wireless communication and mobile terminal technologies develop, the mobility of consumers rapidly increases. The consumers in this dynamic environment also want to connect their devices and to receive seamless services anywhere, anytime. Network mobility (NEMO) proposed by IETF focuses on the condition where the entire network moves. However, in the (NEMO) basic support protocol', the tunneling overheads increase and the pinball-routing problem occurs as the levels of nesting of a mobile network increase. Therefore, we propose a fast handoff solution to support real-time applications even if the levels of nesting of a mobile network are dynamically changed.

articleTitle: A Study on Adaptive Modulation of Pre-coded OFDM combined with Error Correcting Code
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In OFDM transmission, it is possible to adoptively control transmission scheme of each sub-carrier according to the transmission channel because each sub-carrier in OFDM is orthogonally arranged in frequency domain. Although this sub-carrier independent adaptive modulation scheme is very efficient, it is necessary to transmit allocation information of modulation scheme, coding scheme and so on. In order to reduce transmission of extra information, use of a pre-coded OFDM transmission is very effective[1]. In this paper, adaptive determination of modulation scheme and coding rate of pre-coded OFDM transmission is proposed in order to improve transmission under power-line channels.

articleTitle: TV-program Selection with Performer Representative Faces for Personal Video Recorders
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: We propose a new method for TV-program selection on personal video recorders. In this method, performer representative faces are aligned for each program on a TV- program listing to show performers' appearance with their facial expressions, hair-style and makeup. Video clips are linked to the representative faces to allow users to confirm their act. Users can grasp performers at a glance and easily imagine their roles with this intuitive and rich representation. The TV-program listing and the video clips with the performer representative faces are created from video sequences by automatic face detection and grouping. On five-scale evaluation, the proposed method receives 3.8 points on average outperforming the conventional text based method by 1.4 point, which is statistically significant. This shows that TV-programs selection with the proposed method is sufficiently effective.

articleTitle: 3D Recursive Search Block Matching on Graphics Processing Unit
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Motion estimation is an essential part in many video processing systems. The 3D recursive search block matching is the first affordable motion estimator at the consumer level and has already been used in many CE devices. This paper reveals the realization of this recursive algorithm on a graphics processing unit with a parallel architecture.

articleTitle: Using TCP-feedback to Optimize Transcoding Performance
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: A method is described to control a video transcoder based on the actual network conditions in a home network. A single TCP connection is used for transport, where the TCP protocol buffer of the sender provides feedback to the transcoder.

articleTitle: Simple Bass Equalizer for Closed-Box Loudspeaker Subwoofers
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Simple bass equalizer for closed-box loudspeaker subwoofers is proposed, consisting of a second-order low-pass filter with a low enough (e.g. 30 Hz) corner frequency, and with Q factor equal to Qtc of the closed-box. It is intended to be used with a closed-box loudspeaker with Qtc between 0.577 and 1, and corner frequency f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> higher than that of the said low-pass filter.

articleTitle: Noise-Robust Reduction Scheme over Pervasive Home Network Systems Environment for Internet Telephony Service
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents robust noisy signal reduction method for single micro-phone based internet telephony service. In order to reduce background noisy signal without speech distortion efficiently on pervasive home network systems environment, we provide Wiener filtering based new reduction technique which is based on input-SNR estimation method with post-processing on smart devices.

articleTitle: Fast Deblocking Algorithm Apt to Video Streaming Application in Mobile Devices
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper introduces a new deblocking algorithm which can remove the blockiness without blurring the image details. Due to its low computational complexity, the algorithm can be applied to video streaming application with mobile devices. Through the simulation with mobile devices, we show that our algorithm can successfully reduce the blocking artifacts without excessive blurring.

articleTitle: New Medium Idle Time Via Industry Protocol Type
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: WiMedia UWB platform consists of two specifications; WiMedia MAC and PHY. WiMedia MAC may give support to allow industry protocol applications to share UWB resource. Actually, in addition to certified wireless USB, wireless 1394 and TCP/IP, many other industry protocols can reside on top of the WiMedia UWB platform. Thus the mechanism to decide medium access time between them is very important to support QoS. However current WiMedia MAC only defines differentiated medium access idle time via Access Categories(ACs) for traffic data type. The medium access idle time by the ACs may not guarantee QoS for multiple industry protocol applications. For example, if two industry protocols, wireless USB and wireless 1394, use the same AC by same traffic data type, the protocols may easily have contention collision due to same idle time through same AC, because ACs decide medium idle time. Within WiMedia MAC specification, all application devices shall wait for specific idle time called Arbitration Interframe Space(AIFS), which is defined by ACs and PCA parameters, before accessing the shared medium. After AIFS duration, devices can transmit data on the shared medium. Since same AC has the same AIFS Duration, in the multiple industry protocol environments, an idle time via the ACs may be very inadequate for a medium access QoS. In this paper, we concentrate on defining an industry protocol-based AIFS parameter for a new medium access method. The values of industry protocol-based AIFS parameters are determined by priority of industry protocol applications. End user can set the priority of an industry protocol for its own use case.

articleTitle: Playback Signal Processing System Using Waveform Correction for High Density Optical Disc
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: The new playback signal processing system which can play back the large-capacity optical disc over 25 GB in the same optical system as Blu-ray Disc of current state has been developed. Generally, as a capacity of optical disc increases, a read-out signal of minimum pits is remarkably degraded. The proposed system consists of PRML circuit and the waveform correction circuit that only controls a read-out signal of minimum pits. As the result of BER measurements on the playback of 30 GB optical disc, a better BER performance was obtained.

articleTitle: A Multi-Standards HDTV Video Decoder for Blu-Ray Disc Standard
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents an HDTV video decoder core that is is able to decode MPEG-2, MPEG-4 AVC and VC-1 formats and is fully compatible with the Blu-ray Disc standard. A novel re-configurable architecture is adopted to achieve reduced hardware, and a data compression method suitable for all video decoding standards is applied to reduce memory data usage and access bandwidth. The circuit volume of the core is 1.5 Mgates with 90 nm CMOS technology and operation clock frequency is 162 MHz for 1080 i at 30 fr/s.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Forward Error Correcting Codes in IPTV
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In recent years the forward error correction (FEC) schemes at the binary erasure channel have been researched for many applications including DVB-H and IPTV systems. In most cases the packet-level FEC strategies are implemented by either Reed-Solomon (RS) codes at the link layer or Raptor codes at the application layer. Recently an enhanced decoding method for RS codes was presented. In this paper we consider the performance comparison of the enhanced-decoding RS code at the link layer and Raptor code at the application layer in the burst transmission environment to give a guidance of FEC schemes for IPTV application. It is noted that the efficient Raptor decoding algorithm makes it possible to broadcast multimedia data more reliable and faster.

articleTitle: An Intra-panel Interface for Large Size FPDs with High Resolution And Definition
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper describes an intra-panel interface which can be applied to a large panel with high resolution and high definition. For good signal integrity and low electro-magnetic interference level, four level signaling is used. And to reduce PCB size, point to point signaling is used. The interface supports WUXGA, 12 bit color depth panel which has larger than 30 inch size. It is designed with a 0.18 um CMOS process. And measurements show it works properly in 25 cm long PCB, which is the same condition of 30 inch panel size.

articleTitle: On-line Music Beat Tracking with Kalman Filtering and Probability Data Association (KF-PDA)
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: An on-line music beat tracking algorithm with Kalman filtering (KF) and probability data association (PDA) is proposed. The KF-PDA method not only estimates the music tempo and beat pulse positions in real-time but also provides a temporal metrical unit for human-perception-like processing. The superior performance of the proposed KF-PDA beat tracking system is demonstrated using the MIREX beat tracking competition's practice data set.

articleTitle: A User-friendly Video Camera Based on Ergonomic Studies
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: To design an ergonomically user-friendly video camera, electromyograms (EMGs) at six muscle locations were measured to find an optimal grip angle. Grip angle is an important factor in the usability of general consumer electronic products. The results indicated that vertically-gripped cameras, where the grip angle is large from the axis of the lens alignment, reduced muscular load. Particularly a grip angle from 105deg to 135deg produced little fatigue. In consideration of our results, we developed a compact and lightweight video camera with a grip angle of 105deg based on ergonomic methodology.

articleTitle: An Effective Color Distortion and Noise Reduction for Unsharp Masking in LCD Display
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: Unsharp masking (UM) is a popular image enhancement technique. In general, applying UM to each color component independently can produce color distortion in a color image. In this paper, we propose a novel image enhancement technique exploiting the subpixel addressability of a pixel for liquid crystal displays (LCDs). The proposed algorithm reduces the color distortion by using subpixel energy dispersion scheme. The experimental results show that the proposed algorithm efficiently removes color distortion and noise of the edges on LCDs.

articleTitle: WPAN Platform Architecture and Application Design for Handset
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: In this paper, we propose a WPAN platform architecture integrating cellular network and WPAN, and we present illustrative services of the platform. In contrast with the existing handsets adopting WPAN technologies, the proposed platform focuses on wireless communication service development considering the full connection between cellular networks and WPAN. In terms of the applicability, mobile game and voice terminal implementation are discussed.

articleTitle: Middleware Architecture of Hybrid Digital Cable Receiver for Cable Broadcast and IPTV Service based on OCAP
publicationTitle: 2008 Digest of Technical Papers - International Conference on Consumer Electronics
abstract: This paper presents a middleware design and architecture for hybrid digital cable receiver (HDCR) which provides both cable broadcast interface and broadband Ethernet interface, and is capable of handling mixed services efficiently including execution of interactive data application which is reusable from existing cable services based on OCAP.
